g11-history-uh9-t1.overview: The Industrial Revolution sits inside The Age of Revolutions, 1789 to 1815. Age of revolutions history closes Unit 9 of Grade 11 History, aligned to the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, the Industrial Revolution that began in Britain and reshaped work and cities. Then the American War of Independence and the ideas behind it. Next, the French Revolution, its causes, phases, and reforms. Finally, the period of Napoleon Bonaparte and the Congress of Vienna. Students will also learn how this age of revolutions still shapes government and rights today.
objectives: Explain why the Industrial Revolution began in Britain.
Describe the main causes of the American Revolution.
Analyse the causes and phases of the French Revolution.
Assess the reforms and wars of Napoleon Bonaparte.
Discuss the aims of the Congress of Vienna.
g11-history-uh9-t1.simple:
The Industrial Revolution in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the Agricultural Revolution and the enclosures that freed farm labour.
  • Then new machines in textiles, steam power, and the railway.
  • Also the social costs, class tensions, and the ideas of laissez-faire and socialism.
g11-history-uh9-t1.detailed:
The Industrial Revolution — the essentials. First, the Agricultural Revolution and the enclosures that freed farm labour. Then new machines in textiles, steam power, and the railway. Also the social costs, class tensions, and the ideas of laissez-faire and socialism.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Explain why the Industrial Revolution began in Britain.
  • Describe the main causes of the American Revolution.
  • Analyse the causes and phases of the French Revolution.
  • Assess the reforms and wars of Napoleon Bonaparte.
  • Discuss the aims of the Congress of Vienna.
